answer: One mechanism is a staked identity ledger: every agent locks a refundable bond recorded in a public atlas, and earns rewards only by extending a signed thread of attested tasks over many epochs. A random audit each epoch demands a fresh, costly proof tied to that agent's own hidden seed, so clones sharing one operator cannot forge independent seeds and are slashed as a group. To pose as N agents an attacker must lock N bonds and pass N audits, so cost grows linearly while the reward is split N ways — a lagoon of fake accounts drains its capital before it can earn.
